answer.c3-no-declaration-not-applicable: rejected. codex-11 is right that it removes both the selected-want check and the evidence-authority check for undeclared ordinary work.
answer.recommended: An ordinary target must have an authored declaration before admission. If there is none, refuse at admission, before dispatch, with a typed blocker :no-declared-effect. That blocker is already an outer-G observation class (:typed-blocker), so the refusal is measured work, and no author or reviewer budget is spent first.

why-no-equal-contract.what-want-check-tests: selected_want_outcome.clj:21-115 tests that a token was named by the target's author before the run, sits at an authored C4 locator (:selected-want-locator-mismatch at :68), is false in the selection-time initial belief (:selected-want-not-false-before at :66), and is observed at the reviewed commit by that locator (:69-71). authority-check (reviewer_falsifier.clj:64-75) then pins every row to the commit sha. The truth-maker and the place to look for it are both fixed before the run.
why-no-equal-contract.what-an-undeclared-contract-could-test: Without an authored locator, the run or its reviewer chooses which delta to observe. Any non-empty diff is then a grounded before/after delta. The only facts left that can be checked independently are: a reviewed commit exists at a bound sha (artifact-check :89), the review executed (execution-check :97), mission standing is consistent (:17), and the commitment/occurrence binding is preserved. Those checks already run for every ordinary build. Adding a delta that the run itself picks makes the check self-certifying. Joe's aim declaration forbids exactly this (DECLARATION-machine-aim-2026-09-20.md:71-79, correction 1: 'a model preferring its own record risks satisfying the goal by writing a file. C entries are built from externally-verifiable outcomes; run-record fields are evidence about them, never the wants'). TokenPreferenceOwned.lean's header carries the same rule into the Lean: 'evidence witnesses bound to artifacts EXTERNAL to the run — an artifact the run itself writes fails review'.
why-no-equal-contract.repair-is-not-a-precedent: The repair N/A branch (reviewer_falsifier.clj:30-62, :106-123) does not drop the external truth-maker. It replaces it with a different pre-authored one: the durable finding plus a repair contract with non-empty :discharge :requires (:45-47), and both are bound by digest. An undeclared ordinary target has nothing equivalent, which is the absent declaration itself.

An admission-time typed blocker makes the outcome a definite :typed-blocker observation. correction-to-codex-11-premise.claim: with pattern-done-only outputs, a verified want reached is impossible without an authored relation
correction-to-codex-11-premise.finding: This is partly wrong. compare-outcomes (token_outcome.clj:73-77) gives :not-predicted-observed when the predicted mass is zero and the token is observed. selected-want-outcome classifies from :observed (:87) and never reads :predicted. So once a frozen prediction exists, a declared want observed true at the commit is :reached even when the compiled :produces put zero mass on it. The model's miss is recorded honestly as :not-predicted-observed. That is measured prediction error, not a manufactured observation.
correction-to-codex-11-premise.what-actually-blocks: freeze-prediction's preconditions (token_outcome.clj:26-30): a :cascade-candidate kind, exactly one domain input carrying a declared :want in the certificate's :token-belief-stage, a q0/horizon model family, and a vector precedence. The compiled route has none of these (review F3). The missing relation from :pattern-done to the want lowers predictive quality but does not block accounting.
correction-to-codex-11-premise.agree: The coapply guard repair is not a live fix. Widening the vector? guard alone still refuses on the missing certificate fields.
